title: Bastani
subtitle: Persian saffron ice cream
excerpt: Bastani is the classic Persian ice cream: a rich custard base perfumed with saffron and rose water, churned smooth and studded with slivers of pistachio. It is deeply fragrant and unlike any Western ice cream. Serves 6.
sourceNotes: Bastani Sonnati, traditional Persian ice cream, has been sold from carts in Iranian cities since the nineteenth century. The saffron and rose water combination is the defining characteristic.

recipe.freezeNotes: Store in a sealed container in the freezer for up to 6 weeks. Press cling film directly onto the surface to prevent ice crystals.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The custard base can be made and refrigerated up to 24 hours before churning.

glossaryTerms.definition: Persian ice cream, traditionally flavoured with saffron and rose water and studded with pistachio slivers, sold from street carts in Iran.

content.text: is a custard-based ice cream flavoured with saffron and rose water. The technique follows a standard creme anglaise: egg yolks whisked with sugar, cooked gently with the cream and milk until thick, then chilled and churned. The Persian flavourings go in at the end of cooking. Serves 6.

If you do not have an ice cream machine, pour the custard into a shallow freezer-proof container. Freeze for 45 minutes, then beat vigorously with a fork. Repeat every 45 minutes for 4 cycles to break up ice crystals.

items.prepNote: ground and steeped in 2 tbsp hot water

content.text: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar together in a large bowl until pale and slightly thickened, about 3 minutes. Set aside.
Combine the milk and cream in the medium saucepan. Heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture just begins to steam and small bubbles appear around the edge. Do not let it boil.

Slowly pour the hot cream mixture into the egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly as you pour. Return the entire mixture to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring continuously with a wooden spoon, for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon. Do not let it boil.

Remove from the heat. Stir in the saffron water, rose water and vanilla extract. Pour through a fine sieve into a clean bowl. Press cling film directly onto the surface and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until completely cold.

Churn the cold custard in an ice cream machine according to the manufacturer's instructions until thick and frozen. In the final 2 minutes of churning, add the pistachios. Transfer to a sealed container and freeze for at least 2 hours before serving.

attrs.solution: The heat was too high or the custard was left unattended. If small lumps form, immediately remove from the heat and strain through a fine sieve. A small amount of curdling at the edges can be rescued this way.

attrs.problem: Ice cream is icy rather than creamy
attrs.solution: The custard may not have been cold enough before churning. Chill until completely cold before churning. Also ensure the bowl of your ice cream machine is fully frozen beforehand.
Add rose water gradually, tasting after each tablespoon. Strong brands need less. The flavour also intensifies as the ice cream freezes, so err on the lighter side during cooking.

content.text: Bastani has been sold in Tehran bazaars since at least the 1890s. Traditional bastani carts serve it pressed between two thin wafers, the ice cream bulging from the sides. The saffron and rose water combination is fixed and non-negotiable in the traditional version. Modern Iranian ice cream shops add other flavours but the saffron original is what most Iranians mean when they say bastani.
